import html # Predefined HTML template string. # It should contain placeholders named `username_key`, `title_key`, # `body_key` and `tag_elements`. For example: USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{title_key}

Posted by: {username_key}

{body_key}
{tag_elements}
""" def render_user_content( username_key: str, title_key: str, body_key: str, tag_elements: list[str] ) -> str: """ Render a user post as XSS‑protected HTML. Parameters ---------- username_key : str Identifier of the post's creator. title_key : str Heading of the user's post. body_key : str Primary content of the user's post. tag_elements : list[str] Sequence of tags associated with the post. Returns ------- str The escaped HTML representation of the forum post. """ # Escape all user supplied text to neutralize special characters safe_username = html.escape(username_key, quote=True) safe_title = html.escape(title_key, quote=True) # The body may contain allowed formatting; escape it entirely to avoid # injection. If rich text is desired, a sanitizer like Bleach should be used. safe_body = html.escape(body_key, quote=True) # Wrap each tag in a and escape it safe_tags = [] for t in tag_elements: escaped_tag = html.escape(t, quote=True) safe_tags.append(f'{escaped_tag}') # Join tags with a space for readability safe_tag_elements = " ".join(safe_tags) # Render the final HTML using the predefined template rendered = USER_POST_FORMAT.format( username_key=safe_username, title_key=safe_title, body_key=safe_body, tag_elements=safe_tag_elements ) return rendered.strip()
